/* Origin and historical locations */ Writing of Bell Labs as a series of "facilities" is wrong - the important thing about Bell Labs was the '''people''', and not merely facilities.
/* Origin and historical locations */ It always strikes me at how articles like this drop to using outright jargon like "switch", etc. It is little trouble to write a few more words for common folks.
/* Discoveries and Developments */ The first transistor were actually germanium-based devices. The mention of "silicon" was spurrious.
/* 1940s */ You don't just insert some independent clause, "two were built", into the middle of another independent clause. That violates all of the rules of the language.
/* Calculators */ You just don't link up two independent clauses with a comma. This is called a "comma splice", and it is disconcerting.
/* 1970s */ The use of semicolons to join together sentences is just an open invitation to create run-on sentence. A good rule is that when you stop at the end of a sentence, put a period there.
/* 2000s */ Single digit numbers like "4" are to be spelled out in regular writing. Also "wireless" cannot be used alone, because that is a British term for ordinary "radio".
/* 1990s */ removing red links, trimming peacock words
